claim: The immune system plays a major role in maintaining many physiological processes in the reproductive system.
source: The immune system plays a major role in maintaining many physiological processes in the reproductive system.
evidence: This is a general statement about the immune system's role in reproduction, supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: The composition of ovarian immune cells undergoes an extensive shift with age towards adaptive immunity.
source: We show that the composition of the immune cells undergoes an extensive shift with age towards adaptive immunity.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from scRNA-seq and flow cytometry presented in the manuscript.

claim: Aging causes an overall decreased expression of inflammatory mediators in ovarian immune cells.
source: We analyze the effect of aging on gene expression and chemokine and cytokine networks and show an overall decreased expression of inflammatory mediators together with an increased expression of senescent cells recognition receptors.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis data from scRNA-seq experiments.

claim: Aging causes an increased expression of senescent cell recognition receptors in ovarian immune cells.
source: We analyze the effect of aging on gene expression and chemokine and cytokine networks and show an overall decreased expression of inflammatory mediators together with an increased expression of senescent cells recognition receptors.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis data from scRNA-seq experiments.

claim: In women from their early 30's, there is a sharp decrease in fertility.
source: In women from their early 30's, there is a sharp decrease in fertility, accompanied by an exponentially increase in the odds of miscarriages and birth defects, alongside a drastically lower success rate of in-vitro fertilization (IVF) procedure (Madankumar et al., 2003; Nelson and Lawlor, 2011; Szamatowicz and Grochowski, 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: In women from their early 30's, there is an exponentially increase in the odds of miscarriages and birth defects.
source: In women from their early 30's, there is a sharp decrease in fertility, accompanied by an exponentially increase in the odds of miscarriages and birth defects, alongside a drastically lower success rate of in-vitro fertilization (IVF) procedure (Madankumar et al., 2003; Nelson and Lawlor, 2011; Szamatowicz and Grochowski, 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: In women from their early 30's, there is a drastically lower success rate of in-vitro fertilization (IVF) procedure.
source: In women from their early 30's, there is a sharp decrease in fertility, accompanied by an exponentially increase in the odds of miscarriages and birth defects, alongside a drastically lower success rate of in-vitro fertilization (IVF) procedure (Madankumar et al., 2003; Nelson and Lawlor, 2011; Szamatowicz and Grochowski, 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Age affects the ability of the immune system to overcome illnesses and eliminate different pathogens.
source: Another well-documented effect of age is on the ability of the immune system to overcome illnesses and eliminate different pathogens (Kovacs et al., 2009; Plowden et al., 2004; Solana et al., 2006; Weiskopf et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Immune cells such as macrophages, dendritic cells, granulocytes, T and B lymphocytes are present throughout the entire female reproductive tract.
source: The presence of immune cells such as macrophages (Mφs), dendritic cells (DCs), granulocytes, T and B lymphocytes was identified through the entire female reproductive tract (Givan et al., 1997; Lee et al., 2015), and in the ovaries in particular (Best et al., 1996; Bukulmez and Arici, 2000; Carlock et al., 2013; Yang et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Immune cells participate in many fertility-related processes in the ovaries from follicle development up to ovulation and corpus luteum formation and regression.
source: These cells participate in many fertility-related processes in the ovaries – from follicle development up to ovulation and corpus luteum formation and regression (Cohen-Fredarow et al., 2014; Fair, 2015; Oakley et al., 2010; Wu et al., 2004; Yang et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Ovulation is considered an inflammatory process that includes edema, vasodilation, pain, and heat.
source: Ovulation, for example, is considered an inflammatory process that includes edema, vasodilation, pain, and heat (Duffy et al., 2019; Richards et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Depletion of macrophages and dendritic cells results in a decreased number of ovulated oocytes.
source: Changes in the immune milieu, such as depletion of Mφs and DCs have been shown to result in a decreased number of ovulated oocytes, depletion of endothelial cells, increased follicular atresia, and lead to a delayed progression of the estrus cycle (Cohen-Fredarow et al., 2014; Turner et al., 2011; Wu et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Depletion of macrophages and dendritic cells results in depletion of endothelial cells.
source: Changes in the immune milieu, such as depletion of Mφs and DCs have been shown to result in a decreased number of ovulated oocytes, depletion of endothelial cells, increased follicular atresia, and lead to a delayed progression of the estrus cycle (Cohen-Fredarow et al., 2014; Turner et al., 2011; Wu et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Depletion of macrophages and dendritic cells results in increased follicular atresia.
source: Changes in the immune milieu, such as depletion of Mφs and DCs have been shown to result in a decreased number of ovulated oocytes, depletion of endothelial cells, increased follicular atresia, and lead to a delayed progression of the estrus cycle (Cohen-Fredarow et al., 2014; Turner et al., 2011; Wu et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Depletion of macrophages and dendritic cells leads to a delayed progression of the estrus cycle.
source: Changes in the immune milieu, such as depletion of Mφs and DCs have been shown to result in a decreased number of ovulated oocytes, depletion of endothelial cells, increased follicular atresia, and lead to a delayed progression of the estrus cycle (Cohen-Fredarow et al., 2014; Turner et al., 2011; Wu et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Characterizing the complete immune milieu in the ovary is challenging mainly due to the small fraction of immune cells compared to other cell types in the ovary.
source: Characterizing the complete immune milieu in the ovary, and in particular how it is affected by female aging, is challenging mainly due to the small fraction of the immune cells compared to other cell types in the ovary (Lliberos et al., 2021; Wagner et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The murine ovarian immune system contains macrophages, dendritic cells, neutrophils, NK cells, NKT cells, innate lymphoid cells, B cells, CD8+ T cells, CD4+ T cells, and CD3+ CD4- CD8- double-negative T cells.
source: The combination of these methods allowed us to identify within the ovaries the following cell types: Mφs, DCs, NTs, B cells, NK cells, NKT cells, ILC1, ILC2, ILC3, and several clusters of T lymphocytes: CD8+ (CD8 T), CD4+ (CD4 T), and CD4- CD8- double-negative T cells (DNT cells) (Figure 1B and C and Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by scRNA-seq data and flow cytometry validation shown in Figure 1.

claim: Most immune cells in young mouse ovaries are innate immune cells, mostly ILC1, macrophages, neutrophils, and NK cells.
source: Most of the cells were innate immune cells, mostly ILC1, Mφs, NTs, and NK cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by scRNA-seq data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The average fraction of G1-ILC in the mouse spleen is 11.81%.
source: The average fraction of G1-ILC in the spleen was 11.81% and in the ovary was 42.71%.
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry measurements.

claim: The average fraction of G1-ILC in the mouse ovary is 42.71%.
source: The average fraction of G1-ILC in the spleen was 11.81% and in the ovary was 42.71%.
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry measurements.

claim: CD3+ TCRβ+ CD4- CD8- cells are tissue-specific cells to the ovaries.
source: These measurements validate the scRNA-seq results and show that although present in other tissues at small fractions, CD3+ TCRβ+ CD4- CD8- cells are tissue-specific cells to the ovaries.
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data comparing ovaries to spleen and peritoneum.

claim: At older age, the ovarian immune system shifts towards a lymphocytes-rich environment.
source: The results demonstrated a shift at older age towards a lymphocytes-rich environment that was accompanied by decreased fractions of several immune populations such as ILC1 cells, Mφs, NTs, and NK cells (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplements 1–2).
evidence: This claim is supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 2.

claim: At older age, the fractions of ILC1 cells, macrophages, neutrophils, and NK cells decrease in the ovary.
source: The results demonstrated a shift at older age towards a lymphocytes-rich environment that was accompanied by decreased fractions of several immune populations such as ILC1 cells, Mφs, NTs, and NK cells (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplements 1–2).
evidence: This claim is supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The fraction of CD3+ cells significantly increases with age in the ovary.
source: The results show a significant increase with age of CD3+ cells' fraction (young vs. adult and adult vs. old, Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, p-value <10–2), while the fraction of Mφs was significantly decreased (young vs. adult and young vs. old, Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, p-value <10–3 and p-value <10–2, respectively) at older ages.
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data with statistical analysis.

claim: The fraction of macrophages significantly decreases with age in the ovary.
source: The results show a significant increase with age of CD3+ cells' fraction (young vs. adult and adult vs. old, Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, p-value <10–2), while the fraction of Mφs was significantly decreased (young vs. adult and young vs. old, Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, p-value <10–3 and p-value <10–2, respectively) at older ages.
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data with statistical analysis.

claim: Most of the change in CD3+ lymphocytes' fraction with age is due to a substantial increase in DNT cells.
source: Moreover, flow cytometry experiments validated that, as with the scRNA-seq results, most of the change in CD3+ lymphocytes' fraction is due to a substantial increase in DNT cells at old age (Figure 2C, D and E and Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2.

claim: In the spleen, the fraction of CD3+ lymphocytes decreases at old age.
source: Furthermore, analysis of splenic CD3+ lymphocytes show that in contrast to the ovaries, the fraction of these cells decreases at old age, while the fraction of DNT cells doesn't change (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: In the spleen, the fraction of DNT cells doesn't change with age.
source: Furthermore, analysis of splenic CD3+ lymphocytes show that in contrast to the ovaries, the fraction of these cells decreases at old age, while the fraction of DNT cells doesn't change (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: The age-dependent changes in ovarian immune cell composition are cycle-stage independent.
source: These age-dependent results are cycle-stage independent (Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data analyzed by estrous cycle stage shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5.

claim: Several immune cell clusters, such as DNT cells, ILC1, NKT cells, and CD4 T cells, exhibited an extremely skewed pattern in which most of their differentially expressed genes were downregulated with age.
source: Several clusters, such as DNT cells, ILC1, NKT cells, and CD4 T cells exhibited an extremely skewed pattern, in which most of their differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were downregulated, compared to upregulated DEGs.
evidence: This claim is supported by differential gene expression analysis from scRNA-seq data.

claim: DNT cells, ILC1, NKT cells, and CD4 T cells are more susceptible to female aging.
source: Several clusters, such as DNT cells, ILC1, NKT cells, and CD4 T cells exhibited an extremely skewed pattern, in which most of their differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were downregulated, compared to upregulated DEGs. This may imply that these cell types are more susceptible to female aging.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that these cell types show predominantly downregulated genes with age.

claim: Most ovarian immune cell types show a global decrease in biosynthesis and metabolism-related processes with age.
source: The clusters with the processes that were mostly shared among cell types included decreased biosynthesis and metabolism-related processes.
evidence: This claim is supported by GO enrichment analysis of differentially expressed genes.

claim: Most ovarian immune cell types show a general loss of regulation over various processes with age.
source: Another distinct cluster includes a general loss of regulation over various processes.
evidence: This claim is supported by GO enrichment analysis of differentially expressed genes.

claim: Most ovarian immune cell types show a decrease in cellular response to different stimuli with age.
source: The third well-defined cluster includes a decrease in the cellular response to different stimuli.
evidence: This claim is supported by GO enrichment analysis of differentially expressed genes.

claim: Macrophages exhibit attenuation in immune and inflammatory responses with age.
source: Among the cell-type-specific downregulated processes, Mφs exhibit attenuation in immune and inflammatory responses, along with decreased tissue remodeling and wound healing processes.
evidence: This claim is supported by GO enrichment analysis of differentially expressed genes in macrophages.

claim: Macrophages show decreased tissue remodeling and wound healing processes with age.
source: Among the cell-type-specific downregulated processes, Mφs exhibit attenuation in immune and inflammatory responses, along with decreased tissue remodeling and wound healing processes.
evidence: This claim is supported by GO enrichment analysis of differentially expressed genes in macrophages.

claim: Dendritic cells show a decrease in cell activation and regulation of immune response with age.
source: DCs show a decrease in cell activation and regulation of immune response.
evidence: This claim is supported by GO enrichment analysis of differentially expressed genes in dendritic cells.

claim: Macrophages and DNT cells show upregulated T cell activation and differentiation processes with age.
source: Several immune cell types showed a limited set of enriched upregulated processes, in which the most prominent ones were exhibited by Mφs and DNT cells and included T cell activation and differentiation processes (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by GO enrichment analysis of differentially expressed genes.

claim: Almost all significant nodes and edges in both chemokine and cytokine networks were downregulated with age.
source: We found that almost all significant nodes and edges in both networks were downregulated (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by network analysis of chemokine and cytokine expression data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The most prominent affected edges in the chemokines network involved Ccr5 expressed by DCs and ILC1 cells.
source: The most prominent affected edges in the chemokines network involved Ccr5 expressed by DCs and ILC1 cells, Ccr2 expressed by ILC2 cells, and their ligands Ccl2, Ccl3, Ccl4, Ccl5, Ccl7, Ccl8, and Ccl12 (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by network analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: CCR5 and CCR2 take part in chemoattraction of immune cells in the context of various inflammatory processes.
source: Both of these receptors have been shown to take part in chemoattraction of immune cells in the context of various inflammatory processes (D'Ambrosio et al., 2003; Mencarelli et al., 2016; Proudfoot, 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The fraction of ovarian dendritic cells expressing CCR5 decreases significantly with age.
source: Thus, we measured experimentally the fraction of cells that express CCR5 using flow cytometry experiments, and show it is indeed decreases significantly (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Cxcl2 is an inflammatory chemokine that mediates neutrophils trafficking.
source: Moreover, Cxcl2, an inflammatory chemokine that mediates neutrophils trafficking (Lentini et al., 2020; Li et al., 2016), was significantly decreased in almost all immune cell types (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature and expression data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Cxcl2 was significantly decreased in almost all immune cell types with age.
source: Moreover, Cxcl2, an inflammatory chemokine that mediates neutrophils trafficking (Lentini et al., 2020; Li et al., 2016), was significantly decreased in almost all immune cell types (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by expression data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: CCRL2 is an atypical chemokine receptor that is upregulated in activated immune cells after induction of inflammatory signals.
source: CCRL2 is an atypical chemokine receptor that was found to be upregulated in activated immune cells after induction of inflammatory signals (Del Prete et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Ccrl2 was downregulated in several cell types such as ILC1 and NKT with age.
source: Ccrl2 was downregulated in several cell types such as ILC1 and NKT, although it is mainly expressed by myeloid cells such as NTs, DCs, and Mφs (Del Prete et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression data from scRNA-seq.

claim: The changes in the cytokines network with age were found mainly in the IL-1 superfamily.
source: The changes in the cytokines network were found mainly in the IL-1 superfamily (Il1r1 and Il1r2, along with Il1a, Il1b and Il1rn).
evidence: This claim is supported by network analysis of cytokine expression data.

claim: TNF-receptor Tnfsfr1b and its ligand Tnf showed a significant decrease at old age.
source: Moreover, TNF-receptor Tnfsfr1b and its ligand Tnf (TNFα) also showed a significant decrease at old age (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by expression data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Aging shifts the ovarian immune phenotype towards a less inflammatory state.
source: As IL-1 and TNF superfamily members are considered inflammatory, along with the evident decrease in various inflammatory chemokines and their receptors, our results suggest that beyond overall inhibition in the ovarian immune function, aging also shifts its phenotype towards a less inflammatory state.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed decrease in inflammatory mediators.

claim: Activin A is produced by the gonads and promotes LH secretion from the pituitary.
source: Activin A, a dimer composed of two Inhibin-βA subunits (the translation product of Inhba), is produced among others by the gonads and promotes LH secretion from the pituitary.
evidence: This is based on established scientific knowledge about Activin A function.

claim: Activin A plays an important role in expanding the primordial follicle pool.
source: It plays an important role in expanding the primordial follicle pool and contributes to the early stages of follicular growth by increasing FSH receptor expression on granulosa cells (Namwanje and Brown, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Activin A contributes to the early stages of follicular growth by increasing FSH receptor expression on granulosa cells.
source: It plays an important role in expanding the primordial follicle pool and contributes to the early stages of follicular growth by increasing FSH receptor expression on granulosa cells (Namwanje and Brown, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Activin A activates resting macrophages.
source: In addition, Activin A was found to activate resting macrophages – yet there are contradictory findings as to rather its effect is pro or anti-inflammatory (Morianos et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Decreased expression of Inhba and Acvr2a by ovarian macrophages at older age might suggest a specific role of macrophages in supporting follicular growth via Activin secretion during the estrous cycle.
source: Decreased expression of both Inhba and Acvr2a by ovarian macrophages at older age might suggest a specific role of macrophages in supporting follicular growth (via Activin secretion) during the estrous cycle, which decays as age progresses.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the observed decrease in Inhba and Acvr2a expression.

claim: Macrophages may participate in inducing an inflammatory environment as part of the ovulation process as a response to Activin.
source: Moreover, these results may present a mechanism in which macrophages are participating in inducing an inflammatory environment as part of the ovulation process as a response to Activin.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the role of macrophages in ovulation.

claim: Cell senescence is an irreversible state of growth arrest.
source: Inducing cell senescence, which is an irreversible state of growth arrest, is a mechanism the body uses to handle cell stress which can accumulate during aging (Campisi and d'Adda di Fagagna, 2007) and may result in chronic diseases and tissue dysfunction (Muñoz-Espín and Serrano, 2014; Ovadya and Krizhanovsky, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Cell senescence may result in chronic diseases and tissue dysfunction.
source: Inducing cell senescence, which is an irreversible state of growth arrest, is a mechanism the body uses to handle cell stress which can accumulate during aging (Campisi and d'Adda di Fagagna, 2007) and may result in chronic diseases and tissue dysfunction (Muñoz-Espín and Serrano, 2014; Ovadya and Krizhanovsky, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Senescent cells create an inflammatory environment by secreting inflammatory cytokines, chemokines, growth factors, and extracellular remodeling factors.
source: One of the main molecular features of senescent cells is the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), in which the senescent cells create an inflammatory environment by secreting inflammatory cytokines, chemokines, growth factors, extracellular remodeling factors, and more (Prata et al., 2018; Song et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Immune cells respond to SASP factors and clear senescent cells by phagocytosis or killing.
source: Immune cells respond to these factors, detect specific markers expression or their absence on the senescent cells' membrane and clear them either by phagocytosis (by Mφs, for example) or by killing (by NTs or NK cells for example) (Song et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The fraction of old macrophages that express Ccr2, Csf2ra, and Csf1r is significantly higher than in young macrophages.
source: We found that the fraction of cells that express Ccr2, Csf2ra, and Csf1r, which are all receptors for known SASP proteins (Rhinn et al., 2019; Song et al., 2020), was significantly higher in old Mφs.
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression analysis from scRNA-seq data.

claim: The fraction of old macrophages that express Ighm and Clec4a2-3 is elevated.
source: In addition, the fraction of old Mφs that express cell surface markers that were previously reported to take part in the recognition of senescent cells, such as membrane IgM's (Ighm) and C-type lectin receptors (Clec4a2-3) (Burton and Stolzing, 2018) was also elevated.
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression analysis from scRNA-seq data.

claim: Old neutrophils and macrophages showed upregulated expression of Ifngr1.
source: Moreover, old NTs and Mφs showed upregulated expression of Ifngr1 (Figure 4A), a part of the IFNγ receptor, while the cytokine itself is overexpressed by senescent cells (Lujambio et al., 2013; Pan et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: IFNγ is overexpressed by senescent cells.
source: Moreover, old NTs and Mφs showed upregulated expression of Ifngr1 (Figure 4A), a part of the IFNγ receptor, while the cytokine itself is overexpressed by senescent cells (Lujambio et al., 2013; Pan et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Six SASP receptors were significantly overexpressed by old macrophages.
source: In total, we found six SASP receptors that were significantly overexpressed by old Mφs.
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression analysis from scRNA-seq data.

claim: The probability that six genes would be significantly modulated out of a list of 24 random genes is low (FDR = 10–12).
source: The probability that six genes would be significantly modulated (p<0.01) out of a list of 24 random genes is low (FDR = 10–12, Figure 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis shown in Figure 5.

claim: Old macrophages and neutrophils present significantly elevated fractions of cells expressing SASP receptors.
source: Moreover, across all cell types, only old Mφs and NTs presented a significant elevated fractions of cells expressing SASP receptors (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: SASP receptors expression levels in ovarian macrophages are not altered at old age.
source: Results show that SASP receptors expression in ovarian Mφs is not altered at old age (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by expression analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Old neutrophils exhibited elevated fractions of Ccr1, a receptor for several SASP chemokines.
source: NTs also exhibited elevated fractions of Ccr1, a receptor for several SASP chemokines (Coppé et al., 2010), while old NKT cells had higher levels of Cd74, a receptor for MIF, another SASP member (Coppé et al., 2010; Kim et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression analysis from scRNA-seq data.

claim: Old NKT cells had higher levels of Cd74, a receptor for MIF.
source: NTs also exhibited elevated fractions of Ccr1, a receptor for several SASP chemokines (Coppé et al., 2010), while old NKT cells had higher levels of Cd74, a receptor for MIF, another SASP member (Coppé et al., 2010; Kim et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression analysis from scRNA-seq data.

claim: CXCR6 is a mediator of senescence control in the liver by CD4 T and NKT cells.
source: CXCR6 is another novel mediator of senescence control which was recently discovered as part of senescence surveillance in the liver by CD4 T and NKT cells (Mossanen et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Cxcr6 expression was increased in old macrophages.
source: Cxcr6 expression was also increased in old Mφs.
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression analysis from scRNA-seq data.

claim: DNT cells in the blood or lymph nodes consist of 1–5% out of all the lymphocytes.
source: Other identified DNT cells, in the blood or lymph nodes, for example, consist of 1–5% out of all the lymphocytes (Hillhouse and Lesage, 2013; Juvet and Zhang, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Double-negative T cells are the most common lymphocyte across the female mice uterus and cervix.
source: Double-negative T cells were found to be the most common lymphocyte across the female mice uterus and cervix (Johansson and Lycke, 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: DNT cells in the uterus and cervix have a regulatory function and show no proliferation.
source: These cells were shown to have a regulatory function, showed no proliferation, inhibited the proliferation of splenic T cells when co-cultured together in vitro, and their origin was suggested to be extrathymic.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature (implied from context).

claim: DNT cells in the uterus and cervix inhibit the proliferation of splenic T cells when co-cultured together in vitro.
source: These cells were shown to have a regulatory function, showed no proliferation, inhibited the proliferation of splenic T cells when co-cultured together in vitro, and their origin was suggested to be extrathymic.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature (implied from context).

claim: The origin of DNT cells in the uterus and cervix was suggested to be extrathymic.
source: These cells were shown to have a regulatory function, showed no proliferation, inhibited the proliferation of splenic T cells when co-cultured together in vitro, and their origin was suggested to be extrathymic.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature (implied from context).

claim: The DNT population in the ovary shows almost no expression of classical thymocytes development markers at the double-negative stages.
source: The DNT population we observed in the ovary, showed almost no expression of classical thymocytes development markers at the double-negative stages such as Notch1, Socs3, Dtx1, Hes1, and more (Puthier et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression analysis from scRNA-seq data.

claim: DNT cells in peripheral blood or lymphoid organs have a suppressive role and assist in preventing allograft rejection and autoimmune responses.
source: Other studies showed that DNT cells in peripheral blood or lymphoid organs have a suppressive role and assist in preventing allograft rejection and autoimmune responses (Hillhouse et al., 2013; Juvet and Zhang, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: DNT cells may be the result of down-regulation of CD4 and CD8 due to chronic stimulation.
source: Some studies suggest that DNT cells are the result of down-regulation of CD4 and CD8 due to chronic stimulation (Rodríguez-Rodríguez et al., 2015; Grishkan et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The ovaries present ongoing cycles of inflammation processes in each ovulation, which may result in chronic stimulation of ovarian T cells.
source: The ovaries present ongoing cycles of inflammation processes in each ovulation, which may result in chronic stimulation of ovarian T cells and may be consistent with an increase of CD4 T cells after estropause (Lliberos et al., 2021).
evidence: This is an inference based on the known inflammatory nature of ovulation and the observed T cell changes.

claim: Enrichment in CD3+ lymphocytes in the ovary is associated with poor follicular reserve.
source: Furthermore, enrichment in CD3+ lymphocytes in the ovary was found to be associated with poor follicular reserve (Jasti et al., 2012) and thus may have an impact on ovarian autoimmune diseases.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: One of the characteristics of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is an abnormal T lymphocyte milieu that is suspected to be involved in disease pathogenesis and ovarian dysfunction that leads to infertility.
source: Moreover, one of the characteristics of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is an abnormal T lymphocyte milieu that is suspected to be involved in disease pathogenesis and ovarian dysfunction that leads to infertility (Li et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Age-dependent changes in the T lymphocytes population may be involved in improper immune regulation in the ovary and lead to infertility.
source: Similarly, our results indicate an age-dependent change in the T lymphocytes population that may be involved in improper immune regulation in the ovary and hence lead to infertility.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the observed T cell changes and their potential impact on fertility.

claim: ILC1 cells are the largest population in the young mouse ovaries.
source: In addition, ILC1 cells are the largest population in the young mouse ovaries, and the second largest in the old ovaries, after the DNT population.
evidence: This claim is supported by scRNA-seq data on cell type composition.

claim: ILC1 cells are the second largest population in the old mouse ovaries, after the DNT population.
source: In addition, ILC1 cells are the largest population in the young mouse ovaries, and the second largest in the old ovaries, after the DNT population.
evidence: This claim is supported by scRNA-seq data on cell type composition.

claim: ILC1 cells have weak-to-no cytotoxic capabilities and are more similar to Th1 cells in their function.
source: As opposed to NK cells, ILC1 have weak-to-no cytotoxic capabilities, and are more similar to Th1 cells in their function, that is, inducing type 1 immune response against intracellular pathogens and inflammatory responses (Vivier et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: ILC1 cells take part in the process of tissue remodelling.
source: In addition, ILC1 cells take part in the process of tissue remodelling (Jowett et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: ILC1 distribution is elevated in the epididymal adipose of male mouse testis.
source: Interestingly, ILC1 distribution was also found to be elevated in the epididymal adipose of male mouse testis (Boulenouar et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The ovaries may use ILC1 cells as orchestrators of other cell types participating in tissue remodeling processes.
source: As a dynamic, constantly changing environment, the ovaries, which involve cycles of developing and regressing structures, may use ILC1 cells as orchestrators of other cell types participating in these processes.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the role of ILC1 cells in the ovary based on their known functions.

claim: A decline in the macrophages population with age may result in fertility deterioration because of impaired ovarian vasculature.
source: Our results also show a decline in the macrophages population with age, which may result in fertility deterioration because of impaired ovarian vasculature (Turner et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by data showing decreased macrophages and a citation to published literature.

claim: A state of general attenuation and unresponsiveness is emerging in ovarian immune cells with age.
source: Taking together the observed changes in global processes and expression of immune mediators such as chemokines and cytokines, a state of general attenuation and unresponsiveness is emerging.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed changes in gene expression and biological processes.

claim: Immune cells exhibit lower levels of metabolism-related processes with age.
source: GO enrichment analysis of joint processes for several cell types present a decrease in general activity, in which immune cells exhibit lower levels of metabolism-related processes accompanied by decreased responsiveness to different stimuli and loss of regulation over various processes.
evidence: This claim is supported by GO enrichment analysis of differentially expressed genes.

claim: Immune cells exhibit decreased responsiveness to different stimuli with age.
source: GO enrichment analysis of joint processes for several cell types present a decrease in general activity, in which immune cells exhibit lower levels of metabolism-related processes accompanied by decreased responsiveness to different stimuli and loss of regulation over various processes.
evidence: This claim is supported by GO enrichment analysis of differentially expressed genes.

claim: Immune cells exhibit loss of regulation over various processes with age.
source: GO enrichment analysis of joint processes for several cell types present a decrease in general activity, in which immune cells exhibit lower levels of metabolism-related processes accompanied by decreased responsiveness to different stimuli and loss of regulation over various processes.
evidence: This claim is supported by GO enrichment analysis of differentially expressed genes.

claim: Decreased expression of Inhba and Acvr2a by macrophages at old age might be connected to impaired or decreased follicles growth.
source: Moreover, decreased expression of several members of the TGFβ superfamily by macrophages at old age, such as Inhba and Acvr2a, might be connected to impaired or decreased follicles growth.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the observed decrease in these genes.

claim: Previous studies suggested an inflammatory state in the post-estropausal ovaries.
source: While previous studies suggested an inflammatory state in the post-estropausal ovaries (Lliberos et al., 2021), our results indicate a decrease in the inflammatory characteristics of ovarian immune cells during pre-estropause aging.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: There is a decrease in the inflammatory characteristics of ovarian immune cells during pre-estropause aging.
source: While previous studies suggested an inflammatory state in the post-estropausal ovaries (Lliberos et al., 2021), our results indicate a decrease in the inflammatory characteristics of ovarian immune cells during pre-estropause aging.
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression and network analysis data.

claim: There is an increase in genes involved in senescent cell recognition by several immune cell types, mostly macrophages but also neutrophils, NK, and NKT cells, with age.
source: We have found an increase in genes involved in senescent cell recognition by several immune cell types, mostly Mφs but also NTs, NK, and NKT cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression analysis from scRNA-seq data.

claim: Senescent cells accumulate within tissues as age progresses.
source: Generally, as age progresses, senescent cells are accumulating within tissues (Childs et al., 2015; van Deursen, 2014; Velarde and Menon, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: In the ovaries, aging and senescence are accompanied by an increasing number of atretic follicles and cycle irregularities that end in estropause.
source: In the ovaries, aging and senescence are accompanied by an increasing number of atretic follicles and cycle irregularities that end in estropause.
evidence: This is based on established scientific knowledge about ovarian aging.

claim: Clearance of senescent ovarian cells by immune cells increases at old age to match the ovary needs.
source: Our results suggest that clearance of senescent ovarian cells by immune cells increases at old age to match the ovary needs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed increase in SASP receptor expression.

claim: Inflammaging is an age-related increase in the inflammatory environment that develops over time.
source: There is a plethora of studies that suggest inflammaging - an age-related increase in the inflammatory environment that develops over time (Ferrucci and Fabbri, 2018; Franceschi et al., 2018; Giunta, 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Previous papers that characterized the age effect on the immune system in various tissues have demonstrated inflammaging.
source: Previous recently published papers who characterized the age effect in the single-cell level on the immune system in various fertility non-related tissues have demonstrated inflammaging (Almanzar et al., 2020; Kimmel et al., 2019; Mogilenko et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The most evident change in the ovaries of aging female mice before estropause is a shift from innate to adaptive immunity.
source: Our results show that the most evident change in the ovaries of aging female mice before estropause is a shift from innate to adaptive immunity, which is associated with a dramatic increase of CD3+ lymphocytes, and a decrease in Mφs, NTs, and ILC1 fractions.
evidence: This claim is supported by scRNA-seq and flow cytometry data.

claim: Most ovarian immune cell types exhibit a decrease in inflammatory hallmarks with age.
source: Besides the changes in the composition of the immune milieu, most cell types exhibit a decrease in inflammatory hallmarks.
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression and network analysis data.

claim: Prior to the elevation in inflammatory hallmarks and the development of inflammaging, there is an apparent decrease in inflammatory characteristics in the ovary.
source: Our results portray a novel intermediate state, in which prior to the elevation in inflammatory hallmarks and the development of inflammaging, there is an apparent decrease in inflammatory characteristics in the ovary (Figure 6).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data suggesting a novel intermediate state in ovarian aging.

claim: Ovarian immune aging is not linear, but a complicated process that exhibits alternations between anti- and pro-inflammatory environment.
source: Our results suggest that ovarian immune aging is not linear, but a complicated process that exhibits alternations between anti- and pro-inflammatory environment.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data suggesting a non-linear aging process.

claim: Ovarian DNT cells are predominantly TCRγδ-.
source: Ovarian CD3+ CD4- CD8- cells were predominantly TCRγδ-, regardless of age (2.78% at young, 2.48% at old mice).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 8.

claim: The dendritic cell cluster 3 corresponds to an expression pattern of cDC2.
source: Violin plot of the expression levels of several literature-based markers for cDC1 and cDC2 reveal that cluster 3 (Figure 1C) corresponds to an expression pattern of cDC2, while cluster 4 corresponds to an expression pattern of cDC1.
evidence: This claim is supported by marker expression analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 6.

claim: The dendritic cell cluster 4 corresponds to an expression pattern of cDC1.
source: Violin plot of the expression levels of several literature-based markers for cDC1 and cDC2 reveal that cluster 3 (Figure 1C) corresponds to an expression pattern of cDC2, while cluster 4 corresponds to an expression pattern of cDC1.
evidence: This claim is supported by marker expression analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 6.

claim: The MILO algorithm identified significant changes in several cell types with age.
source: Using the MILO algorithm (which divides the population for neighborhoods of cells, see Methods for further details) we identified significant changes in several cell types.
evidence: This claim is supported by MILO analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The most prominent increase with age is of DNT and NKT cells.
source: The most prominent increase is of DNT (CD4- CD8- T) and NKT cells, while ILC1, macrophages, neutrophils and NK cells decrease at old age.
evidence: This claim is supported by MILO analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: ILC1, macrophages, neutrophils and NK cells decrease at old age.
source: The most prominent increase is of DNT (CD4- CD8- T) and NKT cells, while ILC1, macrophages, neutrophils and NK cells decrease at old age.
evidence: This claim is supported by MILO analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The cell2cell algorithm identified that the main receptor-ligand connections responsible for age differences involve mainly CCR5 and several of its ligands.
source: Cell2Cell algorithm ('Methods') was applied on the chemokines network and found that the main receptor-ligand connections responsible for age differences involve mainly CCR5 and several of its ligands.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell2cell algorithm analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The fraction of ovarian CCR5+ dendritic cells is significantly decreased at old age.
source: The fraction of ovarian CCR5+ Dendritic cells (CD11c+) cells was measured using flow cytometry in young (n=4, mean = 52%, SD = 17.54) and old (n=2, mean = 20.4%, SD = 1.97) female mice. CCR5 expression is significantly decreased at old age (* p-value <0.05; student's t-test).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.
